messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ama sen neden bu kadar büyük sıkıntıya geri dönüyorsun? Neden bu keyifli dağı çıkmıyorsun Bu bütün sevincin kaynağı ve nedenidir?

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ma | adversative conjunction “but” | Ama | but | OK | | tu | 2nd person singular pronoun, subject of *ritorni* | sen | you | OK | | perché | interrogative adverb “why” (seeks cause) | neden | why | OK | | ritorni | verb “return” (2nd sg.) | geri dönüyorsun | you return | OK | | a | preposition marking goal/destination (to) | – (case suffix **‑a** on *sıkıntıya*) | – | UNNECESSARY | | tanta | intensifier “so great / very” | bu kadar büyük | this much great | OK | | noia | noun “annoyance / boredom” | sıkıntı | trouble / annoyance | OK | | perché | interrogative adverb “why” (second question) | Neden | why | OK | | non | negation particle “not” | – (negation inside *çıkmıyorsun*) | – | UNNECESSARY | | sali | verb “ascend / climb” (2nd sg.) | çıkmıyorsun | you do not ascend | OK | | il | definite article “the” (masc. sg.) | – (article omitted in Turkish) | – | UNNECESSARY | | dilettoso | adjective “delightful / delectable” | keyifli | pleasant | OK | | monte | noun “mountain” (masc.) | dağı | the mountain (acc.) | OK | | ch’è | relative pronoun + copula “which is” | – (integrated in clause) | – | UNNECESSARY | | principio | noun “source / principle, origin” | kaynağı | its source | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | ve | and | OK | | cagion | noun “cause” | nedeni | its cause | OK | | di | preposition “of” (genitive) | – (genitive suffix **‑in** on *sevincin*) | – | UNNECESSARY | | tutta | universal quantifier “all / every” | bütün | all / every | OK | | gioia | noun “joy” (fem.) | sevinç | joy | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: a, non, il, ch’è, di – Turkish expresses these relations via case suffixes or verb morphology, so separate words are omitted. - **No MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR** items were detected; all required meanings are present and grammatical agreement is correct.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Turkish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ...
